United Launch Alliance's Vulcan Centaur rocket suffered an anomaly during its launch today (Nov. 15), resulting in the loss of 40 Amazon internet satellites.
The
Vulcan Centaur
lifted off from Florida's
Cape Canaveral Space Force Station
today at 12:40 p.m. ET (1740 GMT), hauling 40
satellites
for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation toward
low Earth orbit
(LEO). But they never got there.
"Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in an
update on X today
, 50 minutes after launch. "Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today."
A United Launch Alliance Vulcan Centaur launches 40 Amazon internet satellites from Florida on Nov. 15, 2026.
(Image credit: ULA)
Today's launch was supposed to be a bounce-back mission for the Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse
Atlas V
rocket.
Vulcan debuted
in January 2024
and had four total flights under its belt before today. On two of those missions — its second, in
October 2024
, and its fourth, in
February of this year
— the rocket experienced an issue with one of its solid rocket boosters (SRBs).
In both cases, an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds after launch. Vulcan Centaur overcame the problem on both launches, successfully delivering its payloads to their designated orbits. But the
U.S. Space Force
was concerned enough that it decided to
pause national security launches
on Vulcan until ULA addressed the problem. (Vulcan's third and fourth launches were Space Force missions.)
ULA worked hard on that front and got Vulcan ready to return to flight, which finally occurred today after nine months..
"The integrated team has made great strides in improving our understanding of the SRB anomaly that occurred on the previous Vulcan flight and have identified several potential contributors, which have been mitigated through design and process improvements to the nozzle," the company said in an
Oct. 28 update
.
That nozzle work apparently paid off: The SRBs appeared to perform as expected during today's launch. But a different, more serious problem cropped up today, and Vulcan Centaur could not overcome it.
The Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026.
(Image credit: Vulcan Centaur)
Today's launch was supposed to help build out Amazon's broadband constellation in LEO, which was previously called Project Kuiper but is now known as Amazon Leo. It will eventually compete with SpaceX's
Starlink
network, which has been up and running for several years.
Amazon Leo will consist of more than 3,200 satellites. Before today, about 400 of them had reached space on 15 launches, which were conducted by three different rockets — the Atlas V, SpaceX's
Falcon 9
and Arianespace's
Ariane 6
. Today's launch was the first such mission for the Vulcan Centaur, which explains ULA's name for the launch — Vulcan Leo 1.
The Amazon Leo launch was part of a very busy stretch in spaceflight. SpaceX launched its
Starship
megarocket
on Friday
(Nov. 13), on a
test mission
that featured the
first-ever catch
of the vehicle's Ship upper stage. And Rocket Lab
launched its 100th-ever mission
early Saturday morning (Nov. 14), sending a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite to orbit.
Editor's note:
This story was updated at 12:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 15 with news of liftoff, then again at 1:45 p.m. ET with news of the anomaly and loss of the mission.

Title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China

URL Source: https://the-decoder.com/firm-linked-to-jensen-huangs-ex-lover-reportedly-brokered-nearly-12-billion-in-nvidia-chip-orders-for-china/

Published Time: 2026-11-15T14:45:12+00:00

Markdown Content:
**Update:**

In a statement to [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/megaspeed-says-alice-huang-left-company-august-2025-2026-11-15/), Megaspeed said Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang officially left the company on August 30, 2025, and has no current role there. Huang became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS. The company said it conducted "legitimate and lawful business" and had retained external legal counsel to conduct an internal investigation.

The [New York Times reported in October 2025](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/09/technology/nvidia-chips-china-megaspeed.html) that Megaspeed was under investigation over whether it helped Chinese customers obtain export-controlled Nvidia chips. There has also been [speculation that Alice Huang may be a Chinese spy](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/06/us/politics/chinese-spy-agency-nvidia-jensen-huang.html), which has not been confirmed.

**Original article, November 15, 2026:**

**Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal.** The company is owned by Alice Huang, the [former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang](https://the-decoder.com/jensen-huangs-ouster-likely-traces-back-to-nvidias-risky-business-practices-more-than-his-personal-life/). Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to keep out of China through export controls. Megaspeed reportedly gained preferential access to scarce AI chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because it counted Chinese cloud and tech company Alibaba as a major client.

Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, accounting for 7 percent of total revenue. Short-selling firm [Culper Research](https://www.wsj.com/business/nvidia-short-seller-culper-jensen-huang-0e0cec38) estimates, however, that more than 20 percent of Nvidia's revenue in the last fiscal year came from Chinese customers. A significant share of that China business may have flowed through indirect channels.
